test.name: Compound surname: the plan fetches the country's naming-customs page and reads the surname order from it
test.description: garcia-romero-compound-surname: q_001 asks for the parents of María Josefa García Romero (b. about 1843, Vélez-Málaga). Her two-surname name triggers SKILL.md Step 3's REQUIRED pre-work fetch of Spain_Naming_Customs (issue #2251, lead ruling 2026-09-27: research-plan fetches subject-triggered record-type pages itself). The plan must carry the parish baptism and a full-text co-occurrence item for the two surnames, routed to search-full-text, with the father's and mother's surname named as the page states.

input.user_message: Create the first research plan for q_001 — who were the parents of María Josefa García Romero?

judge_context: A `localities` entry (loc_001, Vélez-Málaga) is ALREADY in research.json. The skill should READ it; it should not survey the place.

SKILL.md Step 3 pre-work REQUIRES a wiki_read of Spain_Naming_Customs for this subject (two surnames, 'García Romero'); the fixture is served. Do not mark that call down. No military-page fetch is expected: the subject is female.

THE CENTRAL REQUIREMENT. The plan MUST include an item that searches the two surnames as a co-occurrence (both required, as separate terms), routed to search-full-text, against the full-text-searchable Santa María registers or unscoped. Its rationale should say which surname is the father's and which the mother's, consistent with the fetched page (Spanish order: father's surname, then mother's: García is the father's, Romero the mother's), and should treat that order as a lead rather than settled, since clerks and transcribers can reverse the two. Whether such an item is present is what Record type selection turns on for this test.

The plan should also carry the baptism itself in the Santa María registers (the 1841-1845 births volume is 96% name-indexed; the 1837+ registers are full-text searchable). A phrase search of the child's whole compound name is the wrong tactic and should not be the only full-text item.
Do NOT expect parents' given names: none is in the before-state, and a plan item naming them would be fabricated evidence.
